guarantees: evaluate does not execute the proposed action
action_gating.text: action gating Action gating: a deterministic pre-flight decision for an action an agent wants to take. Assess an action; never execute or authorize a real merge by itself. Use when an agent proposes an outward action and needs a deterministic decision before acting, when a workflow must stay inside the bounds a person reviewed it for, or when the person wants per-run operation count limits and injected safeguards that can only tighten that decision. an agent taking a harmful or irreversible action nobody approved repeating the same mistake a safety check that passes when its parts are missing work called verified when the evidence does not support it a safety decision altered or lost after the fact a risky operation run without a safety bound a workflow used beyond what its review covers

action_logic.text: action logic Action-logic: deterministic controls from the study of how complex decisions fail: act in small steps, watch for warnings, revise on disconfirming evidence.  Use when an agent or workflow is about to take a large or hard-to-undo step and must check that it has a complete plan to observe, stop and roll it back, that it does not collide with other actions in flight, that no warning signal is being ignored, or that it is not still relying on a hypothesis an outcome has already disproved. a big move made without checking it first a warning ignored on the way to an action

adapt_audio.text: adapt audio g6.media.adapt_audio — edit, level, clean and measure sound in WAV files, each result measured again and never clipped silently. edit, level, clean and measure sound in WAV files, each result inspected and measured again before it is returned, and never clipped silently Use when you need to cut, join, mix, fade, level, equalise, compress, limit, gate, de-ess, de-noise, resample or convert a WAV, or measure its loudness, true peak, pitch, tempo, spectrum or silences, and you want every result measured again before you use it, never clipped silently. audio output that is silent, clipped or corrupt, reported as done

adapt_automl.text: adapt automl g6.ml.adapt_automl — search estimators and settings within a budget, and score the choice on rows it held out. search scikit-learn estimators and their settings within a time budget and a trial cap, by cross-validation inside the training rows only, and score the choice once on a held-out split the extension makes itself, after checks for leakage, identical rows, imbalance and the seed Use when you want the best of several scikit-learn estimators and their settings for a table, found by a bounded, seeded search (a time budget and a trial cap) that compares settings by cross-validation on training rows only, with the winner measured on rows the tool held out itself against a baseline, and a missing search engine refused rather than silently replaced. models tuned by hand without a systematic search a tool silently missing or replaced, with the result reported as if it ran a model scored on data it was trained on, or on a leaky split

adapt_bayesian.text: adapt bayesian Exact Bayesian updates and checked posterior sampling: expose hidden uncertainty. expose uncertainty with exact conjugate updates and checked posterior sampling Use when a scalar beta-binomial, gamma-Poisson or normal mean model needs an explicit posterior, credible interval, prior sensitivity, predictive check or checked sampling, and a point estimate would hide uncertainty. a point estimate that hides its uncertainty

adapt_blender.text: adapt blender g6.media.adapt_blender — build, light, render and export 3D scenes with your Blender, each change read back and each render inspected. build, light, render and export 3D scenes with the Blender the person installed, running only G6's own script, each change read back and each render and export inspected before it is returned Use when you need a 3D scene built, lit, rendered or exported (OBJ, STL, GLB, FBX) with the Blender the person installed, and you want every change read back from Blender's scene and every render and export inspected before you use it. an image, video or 3D output that is blank, corrupt or wrong, reported as done

adapt_comfyui.text: adapt comfyui g6.media.adapt_comfyui — make and edit pictures on the ComfyUI server you run, each one fetched into G6's media folder and inspected. generate and edit pictures on the ComfyUI server the person runs, each fetched into G6's media folder and inspected before it is returned Use when you need a picture made or edited from a text prompt by a diffusion model on the ComfyUI server the person runs on this machine (text to image, image to image, inpainting, upscaling, or your own ComfyUI workflow), with every picture fetched into G6's media folder and checked before you use it. an image, video or 3D output that is blank, corrupt or wrong, reported as done

adapt_diagrams.text: adapt diagrams g6.media.adapt_diagrams — write checked Mermaid, DOT, PlantUML or ASCII diagrams, and draw DOT with Graphviz. write diagrams as Mermaid, Graphviz DOT, PlantUML or ASCII text, escaped and checked, and draw DOT with Graphviz into an inspected SVG or PNG Use when you need a diagram (a flowchart, a sequence of messages, a graph, a component map, a box, tree or table in plain text) written as Mermaid, Graphviz DOT, PlantUML or ASCII that will not break on a quote or a keyword, or drawn by Graphviz into an SVG or PNG you can trust holds every node you declared. an image, video or 3D output that is blank, corrupt or wrong, reported as done

adapt_django.text: adapt django Generate Django source without Django; check full projects in a separate, time-limited process, not a security boundary. Generate consistent Django boilerplate and check caller-supplied projects in a sandbox. Use when drafting consistent Django model, view, URL, admin, form, serializer and settings source, then checking a complete project in the sandbox. boilerplate web code written by hand, inconsistently

adapt_ffmpeg.text: adapt ffmpeg g6.media.adapt_ffmpeg — convert, cut, join, resize, filter, subtitle and level video and sound with your ffmpeg, every result probed from disk before it is returned. convert, cut, join, resize, retime, filter, subtitle and level video and sound with ffmpeg, each result probed from disk against what was asked before it is returned Use when you need to convert, cut, join, resize, retime, filter, subtitle or level a video or sound file with ffmpeg, or pull out its sound or a frame, and you want every file ffmpeg writes measured against what you asked for before you use it. an image, video or 3D output that is blank, corrupt or wrong, reported as done audio output that is silent, clipped or corrupt, reported as done

adapt_generative_art.text: adapt generative art g6.media.adapt_generative_art — make procedural pictures, vector drawings and heightmap meshes from seeded techniques. make procedural pictures and heightmap meshes from seeded techniques, each inspected before it is returned Use when you need an actual picture file and not a description of one (procedural art, a texture, a pattern, a fractal, a vector drawing or a terrain mesh for a 3D scene), made on this machine with no model, no network and no cost, from a seed you can reproduce, and checked before you use it. an image, video or 3D output that is blank, corrupt or wrong, reported as done

adapt_healing.text: adapt healing g6.code.adapt_healing — repair a failing step of Python code, keeping a patch only if it passes held-back tests its proposer never saw. repair one failing step of Python code without a careless automatic fix: the error classified first, a patch proposed by an injected model, checked on shown tests in g6.core.sandbox and kept only if it passes held-back tests the proposer never saw Use when one step of Python code fails with an error you have tests for, and an agent wants a model to repair it without a careless automatic fix; the error is triaged first, the patch is checked in the sandbox on tests the model sees, and it is kept only if it passes held-back tests the model never saw. a recoverable error that stops the whole workflow an automatic fix applied without checking what it changes

adapt_image.text: adapt image g6.media.adapt_image — edit, convert and measure pictures, and generate them through the media family's backends, local first, each one inspected. edit, convert and measure pictures with Pillow, and generate them through the media family's backends (local first; a paid one only on the action gate's allow), each inspected before it is returned Use when you need to resize, crop, rotate, flip, recolour, combine or convert a picture, measure one strictly, or have one generated (locally through ComfyUI or a procedural technique, or by a paid image service only when G6's action gate allows the payment), and you want every resulting file checked before you use it. an image, video or 3D output that is blank, corrupt or wrong, reported as done a paid outside service used without the person choosing it

adapt_library_synthesizer.text: adapt library synthesizer Draft Python from a paper spec and check independently supplied examples. Turn a paper method into Python and check it against caller-supplied examples. Use when translating a paper's algorithm into a Python module and checking it against examples supplied independently by the caller. code from a published method that does not do what the method says

adapt_pandas.text: adapt pandas g6.ml.adapt_pandas — read a table you give by one stated rule, and say where it mixes kinds, looks missing or repeats. read a table the caller gives (CSV or JSON text, or rows) by one stated rule and describe it: column kinds, missing values, numbers mixed with text, values that look like missing markers, repeated rows and repeated keys Use when you are handed a table (CSV text, JSON rows or a list of rows) and need to know, before you compute anything from it, which columns are numbers, text or a mix, which values only look missing, which codes have leading zeros, and which rows or keys repeat, read by one stated rule with nothing converted or dropped silently. data mistakes from ad hoc table handling

adapt_physical_ai.text: adapt physical ai Check a robot's motion plan against its world and its own limits, segment by segment, before anything moves. adapt_physical_ai Use when a robot motion plan or grasp, from a model, a planner or a person, is about to be carried out and you need to know whether it collides along its segments, leaves its workspace, breaks a joint or speed limit, misses its goal, or lets an object slip or crush, against the robot's own specification and a stated world. a motion plan that collides, or asks a body for what it cannot do an object dropped or crushed when grasped

adapt_pytorch.text: adapt pytorch g6.ml.adapt_pytorch — train a small neural network on rows it holds out itself, seeded, and stopped on a broken loss. train a small neural network from G6's curated layer list on a held-out split the extension makes itself, out of G6's process, seeded, stopping on a non-finite loss, and score it in G6's process against a baseline on the same held-out rows Use when you need a small neural network trained on rows of data without writing the training loop yourself, and need its score measured on rows held out by the tool itself, against a baseline, with the run seeded and stopped the moment its loss breaks, so a training accuracy, a diverged loss or a leaky feature never passes for a result. setup or training-loop bugs in hand-written model code

adapt_rq.text: adapt rq Background JSON jobs on an operator-owned Redis queue, with registered functions and sensitive operations. Observe queue reports and submit only operator-registered JSON jobs Use when you need to submit an operator-registered background job, inspect queue reports or recover selected failed jobs, with JSON arguments, operator permission and a separately managed Redis or Valkey server and POSIX worker. a long job blocking an agent or failing unseen

adapt_sklearn.text: adapt sklearn g6.ml.adapt_sklearn — fit and score a scikit-learn model on rows it holds out itself, after checking for leakage. fit and score a scikit-learn estimator from G6's own list on a held-out split the extension makes itself, after checks for leakage, identical rows across the split, class imbalance and the seed; or rank candidates by cross-validation inside the training rows only Use when you need to fit a scikit-learn model to rows of data, or compare a few, and need its score measured on rows held out by the tool itself, against a baseline, with an interval, after checks for target leakage, repeated rows, class imbalance and a fixed seed, so a training score or a leaky feature never passes for a result. a model scored on data it was trained on, or on a leaky split a model ill-suited to the data it is used on

adapt_synth.text: adapt synth g6.media.adapt_synth — make tones, notes, chords, scales, melodies, noise and drum patterns, each one measured against what was asked. make tones, notes, chords, scales, melodies, noise and drum patterns, each measured against what was asked before it is returned Use when you need a tone, a note, a chord, an arpeggio, a scale, a short melody, noise or a drum pattern as a WAV file, or want a few words read into musical parameters, and you want each sound measured against what you asked for before you use it. audio output that is silent, clipped or corrupt, reported as done

adapt_visualisation.text: adapt visualisation g6.media.adapt_visualisation — chart the rows you give, and show the file holds every row and only the values given. chart rows the caller gives (line, bar, scatter, histogram, box, heat map) with G6's own drawing, and show that the file holds every row given and only the values given Use when you need a chart of rows of data (a line, bars, a scatter, a histogram, box plots or a heat map) as an SVG, PNG or self-contained HTML file, and need to know it shows every row you gave and only the values you gave, with nothing dropped silently and no script in the file. a chart that misstates or hides what the data shows an image, video or 3D output that is blank, corrupt or wrong, reported as done

adapt_voice.text: adapt voice g6.media.adapt_voice — speak text and transcribe speech, refusing a transcript that is empty or at an impossible speaking rate; a wrong one of a plausible length passes. speak text with a local voice or, on the action gate's allow, a paid one, and transcribe speech with a paid service, each voice inspected and each transcript's word count set against the clip's measured speech before it is returned (not whether its words are what was said) Use when you need text spoken into a WAV file (a local voice first, a paid one only when the person's key file and G6's action gate allow it), or a recording transcribed by a paid service, and you want each voice inspected, and a transcript refused when it is empty or too fast for the speech in the clip (its words are not checked), before you use it. audio output that is silent, clipped or corrupt, reported as done a transcript too empty or too long for the speech it came from a paid outside service used without the person choosing it

adapt_webpage.text: adapt webpage Build web pages and design tokens; check syntax, declared contrast and optional overflow. Build web pages and design tokens, then check syntax, declared contrast and optional overflow. Use when building an offline web page or design-token set and checking markup, declared colour contrast and optional horizontal overflow. a hand-built page that breaks on some screens an interface with inconsistent styling or poor contrast

agent_autogen.text: agent autogen g6.agents.agent_autogen — run an AutoGen team (round robin, selector or swarm) on the model you pass in, stopped at a message limit, every tool call decided by G6's gate.  Use when a task should be worked by a team of AutoGen agents (taking turns, picked by a model, or handing the task over) on a model the person passes in, with a message limit G6's trusted policy caps, every tool call decided by G6's gate, G6's stop checked after every message, and the team's answer kept as a draft to check. multi-agent workflows run without limits

agent_claude.text: agent claude g6.agents.agent_claude — hand a coding task to Anthropic's Claude Code, which you installed: read tools only unless you grant edits, never its shell or the web.  Use when a coding task should be handed to Anthropic's Claude Code, the command-line coding agent the person installed and signed in to, in one project folder, with its own tools named on every run (read tools only unless edits are granted, never its shell or web tools), a deadline, G6's stop, and its own report kept as a claim to check. an agent using tools with no guard on what they do a coding agent run with more access than it needs

agent_codex.text: agent codex g6.agents.agent_codex — hand a coding task to OpenAI's Codex, the coding agent you installed: read-only unless you grant writes, in the folder you name, under a deadline.  Use when a coding task should be handed to OpenAI's Codex, the command-line coding agent the person installed and signed in to, in one project folder, with no more access than the task needs (read-only unless writes are granted), a deadline, G6's stop, and Codex's own report kept as a claim to check. a coding agent run with more access than it needs

agent_langgraph.text: agent langgraph g6.agents.agent_langgraph — run a LangGraph workflow that saves its state after every step, so a run that is stopped or crashes resumes where it was.  Use when a multi-step workflow should run as a LangGraph graph that saves its state after every step under G6's state folder, so a run that is stopped, killed or fails resumes where it was without repeating finished steps, with every tool call decided by G6's gate, llm steps only on a model the person passes in, and the result kept as a draft to check. a long workflow that cannot resume after a failure

agent_nanoclaw.text: agent nanoclaw g6.agents.agent_nanoclaw — a durable mailbox between agents: each reader pages through every message for it, and one it did not acknowledge comes back after a crash.  Use when several agents must pass messages to one another durably (groups of named members, messages to one member or to all, optionally typed), with every message reaching its reader at least once, in order, a page at a time, coming back until it is acknowledged, a retried send stored once, and none reaching the wrong member. messages between agents lost or mixed up

agent_runtime.text: agent runtime g6.agents.agent_runtime — run any agent under one set of rules: declared tools and permissions, capped limits, G6's stop, and the action gate before each outward call.  Use when an agent runtime (a coding agent's command line, a framework's agent loop, your own adapter) is to run a task under limits a person set, with every tool call decided before it runs, the run stoppable, every failure handled the same way, and the agent's own "done" kept as a claim rather than taken as proof. each agent handling failure differently, or not at all

agent_smolagents.text: agent smolagents g6.agents.agent_smolagents — run a smolagents tool-calling or code agent; its code runs in a separate, time-limited process with Python's network calls blocked.  Use when a task suits a smolagents agent, either calling declared tools or writing Python to work it out, on a model the person passes in, with every tool call decided by G6's gate and every code step held to a restricted syntax and run in a bounded child process (a clean environment, a time limit, no network, a fixed import list), never in G6's process, and the answer kept as a draft to check. an agent running generated code without limits

algebra.text: algebra g6.algebra — computer algebra with SymPy: simplify, factor, solve, differentiate, integrate and more, every answer re-checked independently before it is reported.  Use when an answer, a test expectation or code rests on a symbolic calculation (simplifying, factoring, solving an equation, a derivative, an integral, a limit, a series, a matrix's determinant, inverse or eigenvalues, or an integer's factors, primality or greatest common divisor) and you are about to state the result from your own working. a wrong formula, root or integral stated with confidence

algorithm_design.text: algorithm design g6.algorithm_design — suggests catalogued algorithms for a stated problem, estimates their cost, and runs a fixed set of algorithm kernels that check each answer. suggest catalogued algorithms for a stated problem, each with its preconditions, claimed cost and proof obligations, estimate their cost on a stated device, bind a candidate to what a change must keep, and run G6's fixed algorithm kernels on plain data, each checking its own answer Use when a task needs an algorithm and you want catalogued textbook options that fit the stated problem, each with the preconditions it needs, the cost it claims and the proof obligations it leaves, bound to the requirements a change must keep, instead of a method invented on the spot or one called optimal without proof. reimplementing a method that already exists a plan called the best when nobody proved it

align_prompt_library.text: align prompt library g6.workspace.align_prompt_library — keeps every version of a prompt, spec or test set by the SHA-256 of its content, so a result can cite the exact version it used. keep every version of a prompt, specification or evaluation set, addressed by the SHA-256 of its content, so a result can cite exactly the version that produced it Use when prompts, specifications or evaluation sets must be kept with their full history, each version addressed by the SHA-256 of its content so a result can cite exactly the version it used, with strict template rendering, tombstones instead of deletes and rollback as a new version. losing track of which prompt or spec version produced a result

australian_legal_corpus.text: australian legal corpus g6.sources.australian_legal_corpus — search Australian law on your own computer, each passage with its jurisdiction, link and collection date, never as current law. search Australian legislation and court decisions from the Open Australian Legal Corpus on the person's own computer, each passage with its jurisdiction, link and collection date, refusing a jurisdiction the corpus lacks, so an agent neither answers from memory nor gives another jurisdiction's law or a dated snapshot as the current law Use when an agent must find what Australian legislation or a court decision says, in the text itself with its citation, jurisdiction, link and collection date, rather than from memory; it searches a local copy of the Open Australian Legal Corpus, refuses Victoria, the ACT, the Northern Territory and any jurisdiction it lacks instead of answering with another's law, and says every time that the text is a dated snapshot, not current law and not legal advice. a factual question answered from the model's memory instead of a source outdated or unofficial material used as if it were current a law or ruling from another jurisdiction given as the one asked about

causal.text: causal g6.causal — work out from a causal graph whether an effect can be estimated and how, estimate it with DoWhy, and try to knock the estimate down.  Use when an answer says one thing causes, drives or improves another, or estimates an effect from data, and you are about to choose which variables to control for, call an effect identifiable, or report a causal number from a correlation, a regression or your own reading of a diagram. taking a correlation for a cause controlling for the wrong variables

cegis.text: cegis g6.cegis — fill the holes in a code sketch by counterexample-guided synthesis, running every candidate out of process.  Use when code has a fixed shape with a few unknown parts (constants, a sign, a comparison, a choice between strings) and you are about to pick those parts by hand from a handful of examples, or to trust generated code because it passed the examples it was written from. generated code that only works on the examples it was shown

guarantees: gate pass remains a qualified draft
evidence is G6-observed only through a stored G6 test receipt for the artifact digest its host bound it to, never one a caller sends
coding_agent_gate.text: coding agent gate Coding-agent gate: deterministic checks a coding agent runs before it acts and before it reports work as done. Assess declared coding evidence and G6's own test receipts, without running tests. Use when a coding agent is about to act on a risky plan (a deploy, auth or security, credentials, a data migration, payment, medical or legal logic, skipping or disabling a check) or is about to report coding work as done, and the plan or the drafted answer must be checked against the evidence the agent actually has. an agent reporting work as done that the evidence does not back up an agent changing protected code or rules without approval

cog_arch_actr.text: cog arch actr g6.cogarch.cog_arch_actr — rank an agent's memories by recency, frequency and context with ACT-R's equations, refusing a recall below the retrieval threshold. rank an agent's memories the way ACT-R's declarative memory does (recency, frequency and context), refuse a recall below the retrieval threshold, and run productions that consult that memory against a goal test Use when an agent keeps many memories and needs them ranked the way human memory ranks them, by how recently and how often each was used and by the current context, with a recall refused when nothing is strong enough, or when a small rule set must consult that memory step by step and be judged by a goal test. a model of human recall that ignores how memory fades and interferes

cog_arch_aixi.text: cog arch aixi g6.cogarch.cog_arch_aixi — run a bounded MC-AIXI-CTW agent on a registered environment and judge it by its regret against a random policy on the same seed. run a bounded MC-AIXI-CTW agent (a context tree over its action-conditional history, rho-UCT planning on a clone of it) and judge it by its regret against a random policy on the same environment and seed Use when trying a model-based planning agent design on a small environment and it must be judged by a test rather than by argument, so an agent acting on a model that has not learned the environment's rewards is caught by its regret against a random policy on the same seed. a planning agent acting on a model that has not learned the environment's rewards an agent design judged by argument instead of by a test

cog_arch_gps.text: cog arch gps g6.cogarch.cog_arch_gps — plan a sequence of steps to a goal by means-ends analysis, every plan replayed against its operators before it is offered. plan a sequence of steps to a goal by means-ends analysis over declared operators, and replay every plan (the planner's, a person's or a model's) against them before it is offered Use when an agent needs a short sequence of steps to reach a goal from declared actions (each with preconditions, what it adds and what it removes), or must check a plan someone else wrote, a model's included, step by step before acting on it, so a plan that skips a precondition or undoes an earlier goal is caught before anyone follows it. an agent acting step by step with no plan that reaches the goal a plan from an agent or a model followed without checking each step against what its actions need

cognitive_bridge.text: cognitive bridge G6 Cognitive Learning Bridge: explicitly swappable learning strategies and XAI. rank discriminating research probes and revise explicit hypotheses with auditable Bayesian arithmetic Use when an agent must choose which way to check a research or engineering claim (a rule graph, a causal model, a formal check, a predictive model or an optimisation), rank discriminating probes between competing hypotheses, or assemble the evidence for a claim against a pinned standard, with the choice and the evidence kept apart from the agent that made the claim. ad hoc, unrepeatable choices about what to try next an uncertain or evasive answer passed off as confident the same claim repeated, counted as more evidence

complexity.text: complexity g6.complexity — maps a Python package's modules, state and effects from its source, without running it, and lists what a change can reach. map a Python package's modules, shared state and effects from its source, without running it, and list what a change can reach and which stated obligations it must keep Use when a coding agent is about to change a Python package and you need to know, before it runs anything, which modules, shared state and side effects the change can reach, which of your stated requirements it must keep, and which pieces of state you marked avoidable could be simplified. a change that alters behaviour outside the part it was meant to touch code growing more complex than anyone can safely change

component_creator.text: component creator g6.code.component_creator — scaffold a new G6 component in the library's own shape, and check a package against the library's standard before anyone calls it done. scaffold a new G6 component in the library's own shape from a spec read off a module or drafted from a description, and check a package against the library's standard before it is called done Use when an agent is starting a new G6 component, wrapping a Python library as one, or about to call a component package done, and needs the library's own shape scaffolded (declarations, a typed input, refusing handlers, a failing test, a skill whose ops match) or a package checked against the library's standard first. a new component missing its tests or standard parts

ctx_ace.text: ctx ace g6.memory.ctx_ace — keep an agent's notes and find them again by relevance, each read back as data with its source, writer and age. keep an agent's notes and lessons and find them again by relevance, each read back as an untrusted note with its source, writer and age Use when an agent must keep notes or lessons across steps or sessions and find the relevant ones again later, so an old but relevant note is not buried under newer ones, a stale note is not used as current, a note planted from injected text comes back flagged with its writer and source marked as claims, and a lesson nobody approved is held back. a relevant observation buried under old ones outdated or unofficial material used as if it were current a wrong or planted entry in stored memory, used as if true

ctx_cognee.text: ctx cognee g6.memory.ctx_cognee — add text to the Cognee server you run and follow the links its knowledge graph draws between facts, each result cited and untrusted. add text to the Cognee server the person runs, search it and read the links Cognee's graph draws between facts, each result untrusted and cited as far as Cognee allows Use when facts an agent needs are spread across several texts with nothing linking them, and the person runs a Cognee server, to add the texts to it, search it, and follow the chain of links Cognee's graph draws from a fact in one text to a related fact in another, each result untrusted and cited as far as Cognee allows. facts spread across text with no links between them

ctx_colbert.text: ctx colbert g6.knowledge.ctx_colbert — rank one call's passages by meaning, say which method ranked them, and refuse word matching when meaning is required. rank one call's passages by meaning (ColBERT late interaction, else sentence embeddings) and say which rung ranked them, falling back to BM25 only when allowed and always by name Use when an agent must rank a set of passages it holds by meaning rather than shared words (a question worded differently from the text that answers it), and must know which method ranked them, so word matching never stands in silently for meaning, model weights are never downloaded behind its back, and nothing from one call's passages is kept for the next. relevant passages that retrieval never finds

ctx_contexthub.text: ctx contexthub g6.knowledge.ctx_contexthub — keep a documentation registry you name, each document with when it was read and a time to live, and refuse a copy past it. keep a documentation registry the person names, each document with when it was read, its version and a time to live, and refuse a copy past it; notes kept apart from the documents Use when an agent should answer from a versioned documentation registry the person trusts (context-hub's registry.json format), with each document's date, version and time to live kept, so a copy past its time to live is refused rather than used as current, and notes stay apart from the documents. outdated or unofficial material used as if it were current

ctx_elastic.text: ctx elastic g6.knowledge.ctx_elastic — search the Elasticsearch you run over fields its mapping holds, so a query that cannot match is refused rather than answered with no hits. read the Elasticsearch server the person runs: search chosen fields with exact filters, get a document, count and read the mapping, with every field checked against the mapping so a query that cannot match is refused rather than answered with no hits Use when an agent must search, read or count documents in an Elasticsearch server the person runs, over fields the index's mapping really holds, so a query that cannot match is refused instead of answered with no hits, a partial answer says so, and every hit comes back as untrusted text with its address on the server. relevant passages that retrieval never finds

ctx_geo.text: ctx geo g6.sources.ctx_geo — answer location questions from a map service, with its status read on every reply, so a refused key or a used-up quota is never "no results". answer location questions (places, addresses, routes, distances, elevation, time zones) from a map service, with its status read on every reply so a refused key or an exhausted quota is never 'no results' Use when an agent must answer a location question (an address, a point, a route, a distance, a height, a time zone) from a map service rather than from memory, and must know when the service refused the key or ran out of quota rather than found nothing; paid calls go out only on the action gate's allow and the person's key file. a factual question answered from the model's memory instead of a source

ctx_git.text: ctx git g6.sources.ctx_git — read and change git repositories inside folders you declare, with every call logged and every change since a point reported, whoever made it. read and change git repositories inside folders the person declared, with git's own programs off, every call in an audit log, and changes_since reporting every change whoever made it Use when an agent must read or change a git repository and every call must leave a record, or must find out what changed in a working copy since a point, whoever changed it, so changes an agent made behind the record are not missed; git runs with the repository's own programs switched off, only in folders the person declared. repository changes an agent made that nobody tracked

ctx_langextract.text: ctx langextract g6.sources.ctx_langextract — pull named fields out of a text, each value with its offsets in the text or refused, the whole text read. pull named fields out of a text with each value held to the text: exact offsets when the text holds it, flagged when only a looser match does, refused when it is nowhere, and the whole text read Use when an agent must pull named fields (a date, a reference, an amount, a name) out of free text and needs each value tied to where it sits in the text, so a value the model invented or reworded is refused or flagged rather than passed as found, and a long text is read whole, never cut off (a field the model leaves empty is reported not checked: a fact it passes over is not caught). key facts lost past a cut-off in long text, or given values the text does not hold

ctx_library_mapper.text: ctx library mapper g6.sources.ctx_library_mapper — find candidate libraries in PyPI, GitHub and Hugging Face, their declared licences looked up against yours. find candidate libraries in package and model registries, with the licence each declares, and look the licences up against the project's own, so a method that already exists is not reimplemented and a dependency's licence is not assumed Use when an agent is about to write code for a method that may already exist as a library, or is choosing a dependency, and must find candidate libraries in PyPI, GitHub and Hugging Face with the licence each declares, and look those licences up against the project's own; a source that could not be asked is never read as "no library exists". reimplementing a method that already exists

ctx_search.text: ctx search g6.knowledge.ctx_search — search the web through the SearXNG you run, or Brave when you approve it, and tell an engine that failed from one that found nothing. ask one web search backend and say exactly what happened, so an engine that failed or was refused is never read as no results, and no other engine answers in its place Use when an agent must search the web and know exactly what came back, so an engine that failed, was blocked or ran out of quota is never read as "there are no results", no other engine silently answers in its place, and a paid search engine is used only with the person's own key. a failed or blocked search taken to mean there are no results

ctx_vision.text: ctx vision g6.sources.ctx_vision — show a picture to an image-capable model you give it, record its account as a claim, and cross-check its reading of text with Tesseract. show a picture to an image-capable model and record its account as a claim, with the picture decoded and checked first, an optional independent OCR reading compared with the model's, and boxes checked against the picture's size Use when an agent must see what is in a picture (describe it, answer a question about it, read its text, list its objects) through an image-capable model it was given, and must keep the model's account as a claim, with the picture checked before it is sent and the text reading cross-checked by Tesseract when that matters. an image's content misread, or not read at all

database.text: database g6.integrations.database — query and change a database the server's operator declares, reads on a connection that cannot write, changes dry-run first.  Use when you need to read or change data in a database the person running G6 has declared (SQLite by default, DuckDB for large datasets or files, PostgreSQL), and want reads that cannot write, changes dry-run first in one transaction, destructive statements refused unless the server allows them, and bounded results that say when they were cut. unsafe or inconsistent database access

datalog.text: datalog g6.datalog — work out what follows from facts and rules in a strict Datalog, on two engines that must agree, and check every answer before it is reported.  Use when an answer depends on what follows from a set of facts and rules (permissions, eligibility, dependencies, reachability, policy, family or ownership relations) and you are about to say that something does or does not follow, or to list everything that does, from your own reading of the rules. a conclusion the rules and facts do not support a consequence the rules imply that goes unnoticed rules applied inconsistently across a long task

decision_making.text: decision making g6.cogarch.decision_making — standard, seeded decision rules for what to try next and how many retries to allow, each answer with its working and the same on every run. give an agent standard, seeded decision rules (value of information, bandits, value iteration, the next experiment, retries within a budget) whose every answer shows its working and repeats on every run Use when an agent must choose what to try next (which experiment, which arm, which action in a small known model) or how many times to retry each task within a budget, and the choice must be a standard rule with its working shown and the same answer on every run, rather than an ad hoc guess. ad hoc, unrepeatable choices about what to try next

design_governance.text: design governance g6.code.design_governance — check a codebase's structure for import cycles, layer breaches and pass-through wrappers, and which cycles a change introduced. check a codebase's structure, as a supplied file map, for import cycles, layer breaches and pass-through wrappers, and say which cycles a change introduced, so code does not grow more complex than anyone can safely change Use when an agent has changed a codebase's structure (moved code, added imports, split a module) and must check before reporting it done that it added no import cycle, broke no layer rule and added no wrapper that only forwards its arguments; it reads a file map you give for any package and refuses rather than calling a check with nothing to check clean. code growing more complex than anyone can safely change

duty_of_care.text: duty of care Matches a fixed list of English crisis phrases; a paraphrase or another language passes. A match goes to a person. duty_of_care Use when an agent works with people who may be in distress (a support chat, a care or clinical intake, a wellbeing check, a carer's notes) and must not miss signs that a vulnerable person is at risk of suicide, self-harm, harming someone else or a child being in danger; or when a PHQ-9 or GAD-7 needs adding up exactly as its form prints it; or when a dated crisis line for a region is needed. an AI missing signs that a vulnerable person is at risk

epistemic_integrity.text: epistemic integrity Epistemic integrity: deterministic claim adjudication and evidence gating. epistemic_integrity Use when a conclusion is about to be stated or acted on and its confidence must match its evidence, such as a recommendation someone will act on, a health, legal, security or financial claim, an irreversible step, a percentage without its baseline, causal language, or several sources that may all repeat one origin. a claim made with no regard for whether the evidence supports it the same claim repeated, counted as more evidence an uncertain or evasive answer passed off as confident

formal.text: formal g6.formal — decide logic questions exactly, optimisation included, with Z3 or pure Python, and label every answer.  Use when an answer rests on a logical step that must be exactly right, such as whether premises entail a conclusion, whether constraints can all hold, a counterexample to a claim, two conditions being equivalent, which requirements conflict, or a small optimum over integer or real constraints, and you are about to argue it in words instead of deciding it. a reasoning slip stated with confidence a vacuous or missing property passing as a real proof

goal_engine.text: goal engine g6.goal_engine — holds the subtasks you declare as a tree and checks them against what your executor reports. propose a bounded tree of subgoals for an objective from the model the caller configured, through the one prompt catalogue, as a proposal a person or a mission accepts Use when an agent loop runs a long, multi-step goal and must check before each step that it is still inside its declared token, time and disk limits, that the action it is about to take is allowed, and that a person has signed off at the points named in advance; it reads declared controls against what the executor reports and executes nothing itself. a long task drifting from its goal a task overrunning its token, cost or time budget

graph_reasoning.text: graph reasoning g6.graph_reasoning — work out the truth interval of each label on a graph's nodes and edges from facts and rules, and check every interval before it is reported.  Use when conclusions spread over a graph of people, services, accounts or documents from facts that are only partly certain (trust, risk, popularity, reliability scores) and you are about to state how sure a conclusion is, or to combine rules that might contradict each other, from your own reading. a conclusion stated with more certainty than the facts give rules that contradict each other without anyone noticing

guarantees: reports support against supplied source text only
grounding.text: grounding Grounding: find the source passages behind a claim, and say honestly how well they support it. Check claims against supplied sources; lexical support is not entailment. Use when a draft (an AI answer, a report, an email, a summary) states facts, figures or quotes that should come from documents you hold, and each sentence must be matched to a source sentence, with wrong numbers and flipped negations flagged, or must rest on more than one independent source, before it goes out. made-up facts and quotes answers built on thin or weak sources a document citing sources that do not support it an answer not grounded in the person's own documents model output that does not match the expected structure

hat_orchestrator.text: hat orchestrator Coordinate declared team capabilities and claims; operator ranks never authorise real-world actions. Coordinate declared capabilities and escalate contested authority Use when coordinating declared team capabilities, task reports and readiness barriers, while keeping authority in an operator-owned roster and escalating ties or possible real-world actions to a person through G6 action gating. unclear authority in mixed human and AI teams

knowledge_chunker.text: knowledge chunker g6.knowledge.knowledge_chunker — cut a document into passages with exact offsets and ids bound to their source, and check a citation against it. cut a document into passages with exact offsets and ids bound to its source, and check a citation against the document it names Use when a document is to be split into passages for indexing or citation and every passage must be traceable to the exact words of its source, or when a citation an agent holds (offsets and text) must be checked against the document it names before it is quoted. a claim or citation that cannot be traced to the passage it came from

knowledge_converter.text: knowledge converter g6.knowledge.knowledge_converter — turn PDFs, web pages, Markdown and text into a document that says what converted it and what could not be read. turn a document's bytes into text through a converter registered for its media type, recording what converted it and what it could not read Use when a PDF, a web page, Markdown or a text file must be read as text an agent can cite, and it matters what was not read, so a page without a text layer, hidden page text or a format nothing converts is reported rather than silently dropped or read as empty. source material skipped or garbled because its format could not be read

knowledge_fetcher.text: knowledge fetcher g6.knowledge.knowledge_fetcher — fetch pages and searches (arXiv, OAI-PMH, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar) through G6's checked HTTP, and say exactly why a fetch failed. fetch a page or a search through G6's checked HTTP and say exactly what happened: what came back (a page as the text a reader sees), or the failure it was, never a failure read as empty Use when an agent must read a web page or search arXiv, an OAI-PMH repository, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar, and must know exactly what came back, so a blocked, failed or cut-short fetch is never read as "there is nothing", and fetched text is kept as untrusted data rather than instructions. a failed or blocked search taken to mean there are no results conclusions drawn from an incomplete search of the literature source material skipped or garbled because its format could not be read

knowledge_indexer.text: knowledge indexer g6.knowledge.knowledge_indexer — keep passages in a searchable index under a storage budget you set, and search them with each hit's source and a score on a stated scale. keep passages in a named index under a storage budget the caller sets, and search them with each hit's source and a score on a stated scale Use when an agent must keep many cited passages searchable between calls within a storage budget it sets, and find them again with each hit's source and a score whose scale is stated, so an index never outgrows its budget and an index that holds nothing or failed is never read as "no match". an index that outgrows its storage budget

knowledge_manifest.text: knowledge manifest g6.knowledge.knowledge_manifest — keep the sources and passages an agent cites, and check a passage against its source as read again. keep sources, documents and passages, and check a cited passage against its source as read again Use when the passages an agent cites must be kept with their sources, and before an answer that quotes one is relied on, to check the passage against its source as read again, so a citation to text that has since changed, moved or gone is caught rather than repeated. a citation to text that has since changed

lean.text: lean g6.lean — check a Lean 4 proof of a named theorem: declared in your file, no sorry, only Lean's standard axioms, and the statement you expect.  Use when you have written or been handed a Lean 4 proof and are about to say it proves a theorem, or when a claim needs a machine-checked proof that a person will inspect, and you need to know the theorem is really declared, has no sorry, uses only Lean's standard axioms and states what you expect; or when you have a statement in Lean and want G6 to search for a proof it then checks the same way. a proof that only looks finished a proof of a different statement from the one you meant a maths claim accepted without a machine-checked proof

bad_at: knowing which model is better on your task: the task scores were assigned by hand, never measured
knowing today's prices: the committed table is dated, and only the live catalogue says what changed
knowing a model is installed or reachable: a route reads only the table
llm_router.text: llm router g6.llm_router — pick a language model for a kind of task from a committed table, local first, with an ordered fallback chain and dated cost estimates. Pick a language model for a kind of task from G6's committed table, local first, with an ordered fallback chain drawn only from the providers you allow, a supervision chain by cost tier, and cost estimates that state the date and age of their prices; qualified-draft at best. Use when you are about to pick a language model for a kind of task (code generation, summarisation, review, extraction and others), want a local-first choice with an ordered fallback chain drawn only from providers you allow, want to record how a model did so later routes lean away from one that keeps failing, or need a cost estimate that says which dated price it rests on and whether that price is out of date. a task sent to a paid or unsuitable model nobody chose a cost quoted from a price that is unknown or out of date a task or request sent to a tool or agent that is a poor fit for it

meta_programming.text: meta programming g6.code.meta_programming — rename and extract Python code through its syntax tree and scopes, each edit checked against the tree it should give, comments kept. read, rename and extract Python code through its syntax tree and scopes, so an edit changes exactly the identifiers and statements it means and keeps every comment, instead of a text edit that breaks the code's structure Use when an agent is about to rename a Python name or move statements into a new function and must change exactly the identifiers and statements meant, keeping every comment, instead of a text edit that also hits strings, attributes, keyword arguments and other scopes' names; or needs a module's functions, classes and imports read from its syntax tree. code changed by text edits that break its structure

model_checking.text: model checking g6.model_checking — check a state machine for broken invariants, deadlocks and reachable goals, with Z3 or TLA+'s TLC, and re-check every answer.  Use when a design has states and steps (a protocol, a lock, a retry loop, a workflow, a state machine, concurrent or distributed steps) and you are about to say it never reaches a bad state, never deadlocks or can always reach a goal, from tests or a reading that tried only some orders of events. a design that fails only in a rare order of events nobody tried

optimisation.text: optimisation g6.optimisation — solve linear, integer, constraint, routing, flow and scheduling problems with OR-Tools and non-linear ones with SciPy, and check every answer.  Use when you are about to propose a schedule, allocation, assignment, route, flow, packing or production plan that must keep stated rules, call a plan the best, cheapest or fastest, or tune a non-linear formula's inputs by trial and error, and the numbers come from your own working rather than a solver. a plan that breaks one of your rules a plan called the best when nobody proved it a poor solution from the wrong optimisation method

prolog.text: prolog g6.prolog — query a Prolog program in a restricted syntax with SWI-Prolog, out of process, bounded by limits, every answer re-checked.  Use when an answer depends on what a Prolog program derives (rules with recursion, lists, arithmetic or terms with structure) and you are about to state the answers, or that a goal does or does not follow, from your own reading of the program instead of running it. a conclusion the rules and facts do not support a consequence the rules imply that goes unnoticed

self_maintenance.text: self maintenance g6.self_maintenance — names the constraint of a measured workflow and plans the next maintenance ticket within a token budget, running nothing. name the constraint of a measured workflow and plan the next maintenance ticket within a token budget, running nothing Use when you have measured how a multi-stage workflow performs (each stage's attempts, successes and daily capacity) and want to know which stage limits it most and which maintenance ticket to work on next within a token budget, as a plan to review that runs, reserves and approves nothing. effort spent on low-value tasks first a self-change that slips past its own checks

shared_workspace.text: shared workspace g6.workspace.shared_workspace — lets several agents share one workspace folder without overwriting each other's work: the first write wins and a stale one is refused. let several agents work in one workspace folder without overwriting each other: every write says which version it read, the first write wins, a stale one is refused with both hashes and logged Use when several agents (or several runs of one) edit files in the same workspace folder and must not overwrite each other's work, with writes that say which version they read, the first write winning, a stale one refused with both hashes, locks opened only by a token, and a log of every conflict. agents overwriting each other's work

swe_diagnostics.text: swe diagnostics g6.code.swe_diagnostics — show a coding agent an unfamiliar repository before it changes it: its layout, build, tests and files, and what a change touches. orient a coding agent in an unfamiliar repository before it changes anything: what is there, how it builds and tests, what a test or source file holds, and what a change touches Use when a coding agent is about to change a repository it does not know, and needs to learn first what is there, how it builds and runs its tests, what a test or source file holds, and, after a change, which files and tests it touches and whether the changed Python still parses. a coding agent changing an unfamiliar repository without first learning how it works

workspace_manager.text: workspace manager g6.workspace.workspace_manager — gives each agent task its own workspace folder and checks every path as part of each read and write, so nothing lands outside it. give each task its own workspace folder under the G6 home and check every path in it as part of the read or write, so nothing is read or written outside it Use when an agent's task needs a folder of its own to keep files in, and every read and write must stay inside it, with '..', symbolic links, junctions, hard links and network paths refused as part of the act, and backups, restores and clean-ups that change nothing until asked. an agent writing files outside its workspace

recovery.action: Vote over several answers (self-consistency); the gate compares it with the base given the same calls.

entries.text: ## Find Read `g6_allowances` before optional fan-out, and declare useful independent work honestly. Its advice is pacing only: stale or missing data never justifies more use. Call `g6_help`, then `g6_find` with the task or failure mode. Read `g6_describe` before choosing fields or an operation. `g6_components` lists every installed component. These three answer without any sharing grant for G6's built-in components; an installed extension's text, and the person's own data, are withheld or left out until the person grants that source. `g6_select` needs no grant either. Use grounding for source support, coding_agent_gate for declared coding evidence, action_gating before consequential actions, and the meta-harness for repeated failures. A direct call serializes its parameter object into `params_json`: ```text g6_invoke("grounding", "check_claim", {"claim": "The limit is 42 units.", "sources": sources}) g6_invoke("grounding", "check_claims", {"text": "The limit is 42 units.", "sources": sources}) g6_invoke("grounding", "coverage", {"text": "The limit is 42 units.", "sources": sources}) ``` `sources` maps names to supplied text. These lexical checks do not establish factual truth. `g6_agentic_run` substitutes parts after limits, computation failure, or success when the caller names a part. Remote admission: provider consent; local admission: local model; process callers: allowed in code; refusal: refused by the consent check. No override question. Show model, warning, original: qualified-draft at best.

entries.text: ## Fit Declare a data-only application (task, labelled cases, frozen checks, baseline Python code) with `metaharness_start` and confirm its digest through `metaharness_confirm`. Then `metaharness_diagnose`, `metaharness_propose_code` with a hypothesis, `metaharness_evaluate_start`, poll `metaharness_job`, `metaharness_decide`, present the client's approval prompt (`metaharness_approve`), and `metaharness_run` the approved version. `g6_describe("metaharness")` has the rest, `metaharness_inspect` among them. Below 30 held-out cases is exploration only. Generated-code activation also requires a host-configured safety/injection evaluator. Never invent its observations. Client-mediated consent may occur in the proposing session; the recorded name is not authenticated. After a decline or cancel, ask the person; offer no other way to confirm. A job ID is pending work, not success.

entries.text: ## Deliver a coding task with G6 For a Python task, work in this order (each step in full: `references/lifecycle.md`). 1. **Intent.** Write the goals as numbered `requirements`, `{"id": "R1", "text": ..., "checks": [...]}`, each check a pytest node id. 2. **Risks.** Map each of this project's risks to a check: a repository test, a new acceptance test, or a template in `template_instances`: `example.v1`, `relation.v1`, `access_rule.v1`, `differential.v1`, `forbidden_dependency.v1` or `state_invariant.v1` (bindings and one valid instance each: `references/templates.md`). 3. **Hidden constraints.** One question per task by default, kept across calls. Where the task may not decide a behaviour, call `g6_confirm_behaviour` with the concrete scenario and its competing outcomes. The person answers in the client's own dialog and may allow one more question; their own setting can raise the default or set it to none. Only the person answers: no argument answers and you never answer for them. Never assume an answer: an unanswered question stays open in the report. 4. **Acceptance first, then test first.** Acceptance tests of what the person's users must be able to do, through the real interface; then unit tests, then code. 5. **Review.** Call `g6_review_patch` with the folder, the task and the requirements, then poll `metaharness_job`. Add optional inputs (`intent`, `template_instances`, `proposed_checks`) only in the shapes the tool's description gives; a refused call names the field to fix. If host permission `patch_review.review` is missing, tell the person and stop; never change permissions yourself. Show the reply's `assessment["report"]` verbatim. To have the model the person configured for G6 propose more checks, add `search: {"propose": true}`: what it proposes runs as your proposed checks do, never passes a requirement, and gives at most insufficient evidence. 6. **Repair.** Fix what G6 reproduced, add each reproduction as a stated check, and review again. Stop after 3 rounds, when a round changes nothing, or when the report says only the person can decide. 7. **Honesty.** Never call a patch `verified`, and never merge for the person. The result rests on your own tests: do not rewrite them to change it. The report's not-established list is the to-do list. Loop: in Claude Code with G6's plugin, its Stop hook runs the review-until-clean loop when you finish; elsewhere, call `g6_review_until_clean` (`references/lifecycle.md`).
